name: Fraud, theft, and wrongful appropriation
description: Legal constructs that prohibit acquiring or withholding another's property or entitlement through deception, stealth, or abuse of trust—often discussed alongside moral critiques of covetousness and envy.
foundationStrengthRationale: Near-universal in legal systems; exact elements and defenses vary sharply by jurisdiction.

pros.claim: Gives institutional teeth to prohibitions on taking what is not one's due.
pros.evidence: Criminal and civil doctrines worldwide address theft, fraud, embezzlement, and conversion with overlapping rationales.

cons.claim: Moral categories like greed or envy do not map one-to-one onto legal labels; many thefts are impulsive or survival-driven.
cons.evidence: Sentencing and poverty debates show heterogeneous motives behind economically similar acts.
